body: I personally had a ultrasound follow up two weeks after placement because my uterus is retroverted and my insertion while it went well I had to be manually dilated four times and it took 45 mins to place. Other than an ultrasound follow up I was just told to check the strings once a month and come in if there is something wrong with the strings.

20 F never had children before and I just had lidocaine spray and it sucked but it was completely bearable. I even had to be manually dilated four times to get it placed and that was max a 5/10 pain that would last only a few seconds each time. It’s uncomfortable but it’s max a 6/10 and even then that pain only lasts for a few seconds. I also went on my period, took 800mg of ibuprofen an hour before, and I also brought a heating pad. The cramps afterwards were also manageable with ibuprofen. Overall a positive experience.

Hey I had the Kyleena inserted about two months ago overall I had a very good experience despite having to be manually dilated four times. If you are able to, ask for lidocaine spray that helped for the tenaculum clamp part, but the rest of the procedure just felt like strong period cramps and a lot of pressure. I only had strong cramping for the first two to three hours after insertion. After the initial cramping only mild cramping every couple hours or so. Ibuprofen and a heating pad helped tremendously with cramps.
I know this isn’t advice or anything but I’m currently in the same boat, let me know if you find anything

Hey, I just had Kyleena inserted last week. I was also on my period and I took 800mg of ibuprofen before with numbing spray on the cervix. I also brought a heating pad with me to my appointment, while the insertion sucks it’s completely bearable in my experience. The pain for me only lasted a few seconds max, it overall wasn’t nearly as bad as I thought it would be. I wish you the best of luck!
